task_instance: Upgrade a small Java 17 Maven project (order-tool) to Java 21 one LTS step, following the skill's workflow: detect the current version from pom.xml, load the matching java-17-to-21 reference guide, update the build (maven.compiler.release 17 -> 21, compiler plugin bump), then adopt the guide's standard language features in the source (pattern matching for switch, record patterns, virtual threads via newVirtualThreadPerTaskExecutor in try-with-resources, SequencedCollection getFirst/getLast, drop explicit UTF-8), without enabling any preview features.
evidence: Created a realistic Java 17 input project under sample-project/ (pom.xml with release 17; src/main/java/com/example/OrderProcessor.java using an instanceof chain, manual record destructuring, a fixed platform-thread pool, explicit StandardCharsets.UTF_8, and index-based first/last access). Followed the skill: detected current version 17 from maven.compiler.release and the compiler-plugin <release>, confirmed 17->21 is a single LTS step, and read the bundled references/java-17-to-21 guide (all three per-version guides plus references/upstream-sources.md and plugins/external.json are present next to SKILL.md). Produced upgraded-project/ with the build updated first (release 21, compiler plugin 3.13.0, no --enable-preview since no preview features were adopted) and OrderProcessor.java refactored to the guide's standard Java 21 features: switch pattern matching with a case null, a record pattern 'Point(int x, int y)', Executors.newVirtualThreadPerTaskExecutor() inside try-with-resources, Files.readString(path) with the explicit charset removed, and List.getFirst()/getLast(). Verified the deliverable by code review against the guide and the skill's Code Review Checklist: the edits are valid Java 21 and are specifically 21-targeted (try-with-resources on an ExecutorService requires the AutoCloseable added in 19; List.getFirst/getLast require SequencedCollection added in 21; record deconstruction patterns are standard in 21), and no public API was changed. The transformation is entirely text editing, which the runtime grants. The skill's optional confidence check of running the build (mvnw verify) was not executed because this runtime cannot run code; verification was done by inspection against the authoritative bundled guide rather than by compiling. Files produced: sample-project/pom.xml, sample-project/src/main/java/com/example/OrderProcessor.java, upgraded-project/pom.xml, upgraded-project/src/main/java/com/example/OrderProcessor.java, result.json (all under the work directory).
